components.name: AppShell
components.caption: 01 · Home — app shell, greeting, search composer, saved searches
components.readme:
# AppShell

The buyer app frame: a 232px sidebar on `canvas` with a `line-subtle` right rule, a 56px `surface-glass` topbar, and content on `canvas` capped at `content` width. Nav items are 32px, `label` text in `ink-muted`; the active item is `brand-ink` on `brand-tint` (the only brand fill outside buttons). Under the nav, **Recent searches** lists the buyer's saved and recent queries in `table` text (in V2 the same list holds assistant conversations). The plan block at the foot shows plan, renewal and RFQ usage on a 4px `positive` meter — a usage bar, never a score.

The home state centres the SearchComposer under a one-line greeting in `heading-lg` at weight 400 with one Instrument Serif word (the only serif in the app, and only here). Below it, four saved-search cards with live counts. Nothing on this screen invents a number: counts come from the database.

The consumer provides the nav model, the recent list and the plan; the shell never hides a nav item as a security control.

components.name: SearchComposer
components.caption: 02 · Search composer — V1 filters, V2 Ask, loading
components.readme:
# SearchComposer

The one control that starts every flow. A `surface` panel, `radius-lg`, `shadow-sm` (the only shadow on the page), a 16px query line and a tools row. The mode switch has two stops: **Filters** (V1, ships) and **Ask** (V2, design-only until the assistant ships) — Ask is `smart` and always wears the V2 tag so nobody mistakes it for a live feature. Active filters are `chip.on` (`brand-tint-strong`, `brand-ink`) with a remove mark; available filters are outline chips prefixed `+`. The submit is a 32px `brand` disc with an arrow; in Ask mode the disc is `smart`.

Ask mode shows what the sentence resolved to as the same chips ("Reads as:") so the buyer can correct a wrong reading before anything runs. Loading keeps the panel in place and skeletons the query line; the caption says how many records are being searched.

States: empty, filled, Ask (V2), loading, error (inline `danger-ink` line under the tools row). The consumer supplies the filter vocabulary: product / HS code, certificate, district, workers, source, buyer list.

components.name: SupplierResultCard
components.caption: 03 · Result card — selected, and the sanctioned sample with the 100-character name
components.readme:
# SupplierResultCard

The rich result row, built for the search page (the compact SupplierCard stays for Discover grids). `surface`, `line` border, `radius-md`, `space-4` padding, no shadow; hover turns the border `line-strong`, selected turns the card `brand-tint` with a `brand-line` border and a filled checkbox.

Four bands, top to bottom: **identity** (name in `title`, wraps at 100 characters; then type · district · year · workers · the source-mark row with its count), with Save / Send RFQ / Open record at the right; **highlight chips** — the facts that answer the search (valid GOTS, expiring WRAP, RSC %, EPB exporter), each in its status hue, never brand; **four tiles** on `surface-sunken` (Listed by, Certificates, Capacity, Registers) with an `eyebrow` key and a tabular value, beside a **product strip** of 96px ProductTiles keyed by HS code with a `+N` quiet slot; and, in V2 only, a **why matched** note on `smart-tint` that names the filters the record met.

A sanctioned supplier gets the 4px `sanction` bar and the Sanctioned badge first; Send RFQ is disabled on it. Empty tiles show `—` in `quiet-ink` with the reason underneath; a card with no export lines shows one dashed quiet slot. Nothing is a score.

components.name: ResultsList
components.caption: 04 · Results — header, cards, paging
components.readme:
# ResultsList

The result set under the composer. A header row holds the select-all box, the query as a `title`, the live count as `caption` ("312 suppliers · 1–25"), and the tools: sort (default: most sources), Save search, Export CSV, and a card / table toggle (`seg`). Table view reuses the Table component with the same columns as the tiles.

Rows are SupplierResultCards separated by `space-3`, never hairlines, so selection reads per card. Paging is "1–25 of 312" in `caption` with Prev / Next; page size 25. The empty result is an EmptyState that offers the two nearest relaxations of the filters, with their counts.

components.name: ProductTile
components.caption: 05 · Product tiles — strip and grid, keyed by HS code
components.readme:
# ProductTile

A product line is an EPB HS code, not a catalogue SKU: the tile is keyed by the 4-digit code in `code` (mono) with the official heading underneath, clamped to two lines. Two sizes: the 96px **strip** tile inside a result card, and the **grid** tile (square, `radius-sm`, `line-subtle` border) in the record and the product list, which carries the code as a `surface-glass` stamp in the corner and a source line (`EP` mark · "EPB · exporter page").

The photo is a catalogue image generated per HS code (Higgsfield, one per line, off-white seamless ground so it sits on `surface-sunken` without a frame). It is illustration, and the record says so; in V2 the supplier's own upload replaces it. No photo → the sunken ground and the code only, never a placeholder graphic. `+N` overflow is a dashed `quiet` slot.

components.name: SupplierSheet
components.caption: 06 · Supplier record — side sheet over the results
components.readme:
# SupplierSheet

The supplier record opened from a result, as an 880px right sheet over the results so the search stays behind it. `surface`, `line` left rule, `shadow-lg` (it floats). Structure: a 52px bar (close, "Supplier record", read date and source count, Share, more); the head (name in `heading-lg`, type badge, district · year · workers · register number in `code`, the full source-mark row); a tab strip (Overview · Products · Certificates · Safety · Sources · Locations · Facilities · RFQs, each with its count in mono); then sections divided by hairlines.

Overview is two columns: a plain-language summary and a FactsPanel (28px rows, each with room for a source mark; missing facts say "Not on file" in `quiet-ink`) beside the **contact card**, locked by default — a striped `locked` block that says what is hidden and that an RFQ still reaches the supplier. Products is four StatTiles and a ProductTile grid keyed by HS code. Certificates is four CertificateCards. Safety shows the single RSC remediation % on a `positive` meter, training status, and the five report links (a missing one is a dashed quiet chip).

A sticky `surface-glass` action bar holds Send RFQ (`brand`), Save to list and Compare. A sanctioned supplier adds the SanctionBanner under the bar and disables Send RFQ.

components.name: ProductSheet
components.caption: 07 · Product line — nested sheet with back
components.readme:
# ProductSheet

A nested sheet reached from a ProductTile, with a back control and a breadcrumb (supplier / HS code) in the bar. Left: the grid tile at 320px with a caption that says the photo is generated. Right: `eyebrow` ("HS 6109 · EPB export line"), the heading text, a single-column FactsPanel (chapter, exporter since, other lines in `code`, certified scope with its mark, product list with its mark, the EPB source link), then Send RFQ for this line and a secondary button that runs the same HS code across the catalogue with its live count.

components.name: RFQComposer
components.caption: 08 · RFQ composer — suppliers, product, template with variables, live preview
components.readme:
# RFQComposer

The request-for-quote dialog, 1180px, `radius-lg`, `shadow-lg`. Three columns: a **rail** on `canvas` (Suppliers, Product, Details, Questions, Follow-up rules — each with a count and a `caution-ink` warning when something required is missing); the **editor** with a template switch (First contact / Repeat supplier) and the body as text with inline **variables** (`var`: `brand-tint` chips; a missing one is `caution-tint`) and a product table; and a **preview** on `surface-sunken` that renders the message exactly as the supplier receives it, with missing variables still flagged.

The message cites the record — certificate number, HS line — so the supplier knows the buyer read it. The footer counts what is missing and holds Save draft and Send RFQ (`brand`). Auto follow-up, auto reply and "Improve wording" are `smart` V2 controls, present in the design and inert in V1. The preview never blurs contact details; SourceBD delivers the RFQ, so the address is not needed on the buyer's side.

components.name: RFQList
components.caption: 09 · RFQ list — status chips, table, toast
components.readme:
# RFQList

The RFQs page: a `heading` with the live count, a search input, Fields, Sort and + New RFQ (`brand`); a row of status chips with counts (All, Awaiting reply, Quoted, Draft, Closed); a Table with 36px rows — RFQ name, supplier, product as `code` + name, status badge (`positive` for sent / read, `caution` for overdue, `typ` for draft), sent, reply-by, quotes, action. Paging in `caption`. The Toast (`surface-inverse`, `signal` dot) confirms a draft save and names the supplier.

At launch almost every buyer sees the empty state instead of this table; see EmptyState.

components.name: StatTiles
components.caption: 10 · Stats and tiles — bordered in the record, sunken in a card, loading
components.readme:
# StatTiles

Two small figure blocks that share one shape: an `eyebrow` key, a tabular value, a `caption` qualifier that names the source. **Stat** (`line` border, 20px value) heads a record section. **Tile** (`surface-sunken`, no border, 15px value) sits inside a result card so it reads as part of the card, not a card within a card. An empty value is `—` in `quiet-ink` with the reason beneath ("not on file"). Loading is two skeleton bars. The value is always a fact — a count, a percentage the source published, a list of names — never a computed grade.

components.name: CertificateCard
components.caption: 11 · Certificate card — valid, expiring, no expiry, expired, none, detail popover
components.readme:
# CertificateCard

One card per certificate: the issuer's rank mark, the scheme name in `label`, the state badge at the right, the certificate number in `code`, issuer and date in `caption`, and a link to the issuer's document page. Four states from the data: **Valid** (`positive`), **expiring within 90 days** (`caution`, shows the days left), **No expiry** on file (`typ`, the most common state — two in three certificates), **Expired** (`caution`). The none state is a dashed `quiet` card that says which registers were checked and when.

The detail popover repeats the number and adds issuer, valid until, issued (almost always "Not on file" — the slot exists, the design does not assume it), scope and products, then the document link and the source-page status. No "checked by SourceBD" mark until checking exists (open question 6 in the rebuild spec).

components.name: LockedTable
components.caption: 12 · Locked rows — plan-gated records shown as records, not blur
components.readme:
# LockedTable

A table whose lower rows are on a higher plan. The visible rows are ordinary Table rows; the locked rows use the `locked` striped ground with `locked-stripe` bars standing in for text at the real column widths, and a final full-width row that says how many more exist and where they are read. The header carries the same count and a `locked` chip. The rows are real — the design never invents a number of hidden rows — and nothing is blurred: the stripe is a state, not a veil. Used for RSC safety reports, evidence citations and, in V2, export shipment records.

components.name: EmptyState
components.caption: 13 · Empty, no-match, no-list, error
components.readme:
# EmptyState

The state almost every user sees at launch (7 RFQs, 0 quotes, 0 orders on production). Centred in a `panel`: an optional 28px thin icon in `ink-subtle`, a `heading-sm`, one `body` paragraph capped at 40ch, and at most two actions. Copy sells what the feature does ("Your first RFQ lands here…") and never apologises. The no-match state is different: it offers the two nearest relaxations of the filters with their counts, so the buyer leaves with results. The error state uses `danger-line` and `danger-ink` for the title only, keeps the filters, and offers Try again.

components.name: Highlights
components.caption: 14 · Highlights — what the records say, as popover and as chips
components.readme:
# Highlights

The facts that answer "why is this supplier here", in two forms. The **popover** (`pop`, `shadow-md`) groups them under `eyebrow` headings — Registers, Certificates, Safety and buyers — each a rank mark, a bold `label` line and a `caption` with the number, date or scope and the source-page status. The **chips** are the same facts inline on a card in status hues: `positive` for valid / active, `caution` for expiring, expired or contradicted, `typ` for neutral facts (a register, an HS count), `quiet` for nothing on file, `sanction` reserved. In V2 a `smart` chip adds "3 of 3 filters". Chips describe; they never rank or grade, and brand green is never a chip fill.

components.name: Dashboard
components.caption: 15 · The whole flow at once — search, results and the record sheet open
components.readme:
# Dashboard

The end-to-end composition at 1440px: AppShell → SearchComposer with three active filters → ResultsList with the selected SupplierResultCard → SupplierSheet open over it, scrim behind. Every record shown is real (Aboni Knitwear Ltd, S M Knitwears Limited; production, 18 Sep 2026) and every product photo is keyed to one of Aboni's twelve EPB HS codes. Compare with the reference recording: same journey (ask → list → record → contact), none of its chrome — hairlines instead of shadows, mono stamps instead of badges, sources on every fact, locked instead of blurred, and no match score anywhere a buyer can see it.
